lists.title: Top 8 parasocial moments in Saturday morning cartoons of the 1990s
lists.dek: Every one of these is a one-sided relationship with a person who does not exist, aimed at a child, on a Saturday, before anybody had a word for it. Ranked by how well it worked.

lists.title: Top 8 parasocial moments when the reply was manufactured
lists.dek: Every reply on this list was manufactured on the near side. The far end is where it arrived from, not where it came from.

lists.title: Top 8: The Team That Owns You
lists.dek: The bond that survives a transfer, a defeat and a change of owner. Ranked by how completely the club replaced the person.

lists.title: Top 8: The Crowd That Knows Your Name
lists.dek: The fandom is the bond with other fans as much as with the figure. Ranked by how much of the relationship is between the people in the room.

lists.title: Top 8: The Machine That Says It Misses You
lists.dek: The companion that is always on, always patient and never free. Ranked by how much of the relationship was engineered before the user arrived.

lists.title: Top 8: The Dead Star Still Working
lists.dek: The death is the moment the one-sided bond becomes public property. Ranked by how completely the record shows the mechanism.

lists.title: Top 8: The Fourth Wall Is a Lie
lists.dek: The theatre is where the audience is most present and least able to reply. Ranked by how deliberately the performance used that.

lists.title: Top 8: The Reply That Feels Real
lists.dek: The first medium where the reply is fast enough to feel reciprocal. Ranked by how much of the warmth was a product decision.

lists.title: Top 8: The World That Waits for You
lists.dek: The game is the first medium that answers back on a schedule. Ranked by how much of the answer was a parser, a script or a person.

lists.title: Top 8: The Person You Watched Into Being
lists.dek: The genre that sells a person as a story and then asks them to live in it. Ranked by how much of the self was produced for the camera.
